To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the MAGIC collaboration has set the strongest limits on Lorentz violation to date, with a sensitivity that is comparable to the one of the H.E.S.S. collaboration, and that the limits are competitive with the ones set by the Fermi-LAT collaboration.
the MAGIC observations of the Crab Pulsar do not show a significant energy dependence of the arrival time of gamma rays.

(i) the MAGIC data do not show evidence for a time-of-flight effect in the arrival times of gamma rays from the Crab pulsar, (ii) we have obtained limits on Lorentz violation at the level of 10(17-10) GeV for linear and quadratic scenarios, respectively, for the superluminal case and (iii) we have performed a thorough investigation of the bias of our test statistic, and have obtained a coverage that is close to the nominal one.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the observation of gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) with the MAGIC telescopic array.

the search for the effects of Lorentz Invariance Violation (LIV) in the propagation of gamma rays, and in particular with the search of a possible energy dependence on the arrival time of the gamma rays.
a test of Lorentz invari-ance violation at energies on the scale of the Planck mass, which is a regime where no other test exists.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MAGIC limits on E QG are not competitive with the best limits from other sources.
the MAGIC data do not provide evidence for a Lorentz violating dispersion relation.
the MAGIC data do not provide evidence of any Lorentz in violation at the level of the Planck scale.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the present limits on E QG2 are the strongest ever obtained from a single source, and the limits on E QGL1 are the second strongest.

the MAGIC observations of the Crab Pulsar are consistent with the predictions of Lorentz invariants, and that our constraints on the energy scale of the Lorentz invari- ance violation are the best to date.
the MAGIC data are consistent with the Lorentz in variance symmetry, and that the limits on the effective energy scale are among the most stringent ones obtained so far.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Crab pulsar is a very promising source for tests of Lorentz in variance violation in the future.
, with the present data, we can only place a lower bound of about 10(17)-10(18) GeV on the energy scale of Lorentz in variance violation.

the Crab pulsar is a very promising target for future Lorentz in violation tests with gamma ray telescopes, in particular if a more detailed understanding of the pulse shape in the energy range 100 GeV to 1 TeV can be reached.
